definition_zh: 饿死；挨饿；饿肚子；使挨饿
definition_en: to suffer or die because there is no food to eat, or to make someone do so
core_image: 空了很久的碗还摆在桌上——身体里没有一粒米进来
scene: 战乱中粮车被拦截，村庄接连断粮。People in the village starved during the long winter blockade.
sceneCN: 这里 starve 是「饿死」（第 1 个义项：因缺少食物而死亡）；句意为村庄的人在漫长的冬季封锁中饿死了。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「饥饿；饿死」
由动词加后缀构成，义为「瘦弱挨饿的人」

senses.title: To die from lack of food
senses.definition: to die because there is no food to eat
senses.definitionCN: 因没有食物可吃而死亡
senses.example: Thousands of people starved after the harvest failed.
senses.exampleCN: 庄稼歉收后，成千上万的人饿死了。
senses.why: When the bowl stays empty long enough, the body itself gives out.
senses.whyCN: 碗空得足够久，身体本身就会耗尽，意象的尽头是死亡。

senses.title: To suffer great hunger
senses.definition: to feel extremely hungry or suffer from not having enough food
senses.definitionCN: 感到极度饥饿或长期吃不饱
senses.example: He missed lunch and claimed he was starving.
senses.exampleCN: 他没吃午饭，声称自己快饿死了。
senses.why: The same empty-bowl image, softened into everyday exaggeration.
senses.whyCN: 同一只空碗的画面被软化成日常夸张的说法。

senses.title: To deprive someone or something of food or resources
senses.definition: to prevent a person, animal, or organization from getting food or necessary resources
senses.definitionCN: 不给人、动物或组织提供食物或必要的资源
senses.example: The factory was starved of investment for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂多年得不到投资。
senses.why: Withholding the food is the active hand behind the empty bowl.
senses.whyCN: 那只空碗背后有主动扣住不给的手，意象延伸为刻意断供。

intro.en: Starve goes back to an Old English word that first meant simply to die, and narrowed to dying from hunger.
intro.cn: starve 源自古英语，最初泛指「死亡」，后来词义收窄为「饿死」。

items.en: A reconstructed root *sterban- meant to die or be stiff, related to the idea of the body going rigid.
items.cn: 重构词根 *sterban- 表示「死亡；僵硬」，与身体变僵的意象相关。

items.en: Steorfan meant simply to die, with no special link to hunger.
items.cn: 古英语 steorfan 仅表示「死亡」，与饥饿并无专门关联。

items.en: Sterven gradually shifted toward dying of hunger or cold, especially in northern dialects.
items.cn: 中古英语 sterven 逐渐偏向「饿死；冻死」，尤其在北方方言中。

items.en: The meaning settled on dying from lack of food, and the old general sense faded.
items.cn: 词义固定为「饿死」，原本泛指死亡的含义消退。

items.en: Colloquial starving for very hungry became common, and starve of extended the idea to resources.
items.cn: 口语中 starve 用于夸张地表示「饿极了」，starve of 又把意象延伸到资源匮乏。

note.en: Starve looks like the unrelated word star, and sits near other hunger words of different roots.
note.cn: starve 拼写上与不相关的 star 相近，义场上靠近词源不同的几个「饥饿」词。

entries.definition: a burning ball of gas in the sky, or a famous person
entries.definitionCN: 星星；明星；只是拼写与 starve 相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to look at something for a long time with wide eyes
entries.definitionCN: 凝视；盯着看；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: to begin doing something
entries.definitionCN: 开始；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: to make someone very hungry, now mostly literary
entries.definitionCN: 使挨饿；使极饿，较为文雅罕用的旧词

entries.definition: to want or need food, or to long for something strongly
entries.definitionCN: 饥饿；渴望，强调饥与欲，不像 starve 那样指向死亡

entries.definition: to eat no food for a period, usually by choice
entries.definitionCN: 禁食；斋戒，是自愿不吃，与被迫挨饿相反

entries.definition: to provide food and substances needed to live and grow
entries.definitionCN: 滋养；养育，与使挨饿意义相反

normalIntro.en: Build memory on the real word family and the death-to-hunger shift.
normalIntro.cn: 利用真实的词族和「从死亡到饥饿」的词义收窄来记忆。

normal.en: Old English steorfan meant to die, so starve carries a shadow of death in its root.
normal.cn: 古英语 steorfan 意为死亡，词根里就带着死亡的影子。

normal.en: Starvation is the noun form, seen in phrases like starvation wages.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 starvation，常见搭配如 starvation wages（饿不死但也养不活人的工资）。

normal.en: The phrase starve to death separates the everyday sense from the literal one.
normal.cn: 短语 starve to death 把字面义与日常夸张义区分开来。

normal.en: Starving is how people say very hungry in casual speech.
normal.cn: 口语里说 I'm starving 就是「我饿死了」的夸张说法。

normal.en: Starve something of something means to cut off supply, not only food.
normal.cn: starve A of B 表示切断供应，对象不只是食物。

abstract.en: Picture an empty bowl on the table that no one refills, day after day.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上那只没人续添的空碗，一天天空着。

abstract.en: Feel the body slowly running out of fuel like a fire losing its last wood.
abstract.cn: 体会身体像缺柴的火慢慢熄灭一样耗尽能量。

abstract.en: See a factory wilting when money stops flowing, like a field with no rain.
abstract.cn: 看工厂在资金断流下枯萎，如同无雨的田地。

examples.en: The prisoners were starved and given almost no water.
examples.cn: 囚犯们被断食，几乎不给水。

examples.en: I skipped breakfast and I'm absolutely starving now.
examples.cn: 我没吃早饭，现在饿得不行。

examples.en: The research lab was starved of funding for two years.
examples.cn: 这家研究实验室两年缺乏经费。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死他饿夫」——一家老小没饭吃，最后「死他饿」倒下的画面，帮助记住饿死之意。

root: 一般认为源自日耳曼语词根 *sterban-（死亡；僵硬），古英语 steorfan 原义泛指死亡，中古时期词义收窄为饿死；与 hunger、famine 等词无词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: From the original meaning of dying, the word narrows to dying of hunger, then softens into everyday hunger and the act of cutting off supplies.
sensesIntro.cn: 词义从「死亡」收窄到「饿死」，再软化出日常的「饿极了」与「断供使匮乏」两个方向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty bowl no one refills, until the body burns out
core.cn: 核心意象：一只没人续添的空碗，直到身体耗尽

branches.en: dying because the food never comes
branches.cn: 因食物始终不来而死亡

branches.en: everyday exaggeration of hunger
withholding food, money, or resources
branches.cn: 刻意不给食物、资金或资源

branches.en: the body and the appetite both run empty
the hand that cuts off the supply

intro.en: Starve is a single short root word, but its family shows how one root grew nouns and agent nouns.
intro.cn: starve 是单一短词根，其词族展示了词根如何派生出名词与施动者名词。

latinIntro.en: Starve has no Latin relatives; it is native Germanic, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: starve 没有拉丁同源词，属于日耳曼本土词源，故拉丁同族词列表为空。

items.meaning: to die; later to die of hunger
the state of suffering or dying from hunger
items.exampleCN: 为防止饿死而开展的饥荒救济

items.meaningCN: 正在挨饿的；口语中指饿极了

items.meaning: a thin, weak person always short of food
makes nouns of action or state
items.meaningCN: 名词后缀，表动作或状态

items.meaning: makes nouns for a kind of person or thing, often small or weak
items.meaningCN: 名词后缀，常带弱小意味

items.meaning: marks past tense or a completed state

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「饥饿；饿死」
由动词加后缀 -ling 构成，义为「瘦弱挨饿的人」

definition_zh: 状态；情形；国家；州；政府；陈述；说明
definition_en: the condition someone or something is in, an organized political country, or to say something formally
core_image: 一面标着刻度的仪表盘：指针指到哪里，事情就处在哪个档位
scene: 灾后重建会议上，先读出各项指标。She described the poor state of the city's bridges after the flood.
sceneCN: 这里 state 是「状态；状况」（第 1 个义项：人或事物所处的情形）；句意为她描述了洪水过后该市桥梁的糟糕状况。

collocations.zh: 最先进的；当前技术水平

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「陈述；声明；报表」
由本词加复合成分构成，义为「政治家」
由 re- 加本词构成，义为「重申；重新表述」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「庄严的；气派的」

senses.title: The condition someone or something is in
senses.definition: the general physical, mental, or overall condition of a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物的总体身体、精神或一般状况
senses.example: The old house is in a bad state of repair.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老房子年久失修。
senses.why: The gauge needle points somewhere, and that reading is the condition.
senses.whyCN: 仪表盘的指针停在某处，那个读数就是「状况」。

senses.title: An organized political community under one government
senses.definition: a country or its government considered as an organized political body
senses.definitionCN: 作为有组织政治实体的国家或其政府
senses.example: The state provides free schooling for all children.
senses.exampleCN: 国家为所有儿童提供免费教育。
senses.why: A whole nation read on one dial, run as a single ordered system.
senses.whyCN: 整个国家被读作一块仪表盘，作为单一有序系统运转。

senses.title: A part of a federal country, especially the United States
senses.definition: one of the partly self-governing regions forming certain federal countries
senses.definitionCN: 组成某些联邦国家的、拥有部分自治权的地区
senses.example: Texas is the largest oil-producing state in the union.
senses.exampleCN: 得克萨斯是联邦中最大的产油州。
senses.why: The big dial splits into smaller dials, each with its own controls.
senses.whyCN: 大仪表盘分成小仪表盘，每个都有自己的控制旋钮。

senses.title: To say or write something clearly and formally
senses.definition: to express something in speech or writing, especially clearly and formally
senses.definitionCN: 以口头或书面形式表达，尤指清楚而正式地表达
senses.example: Please state your name and address for the record.
senses.exampleCN: 请为记录在案说明您的姓名和地址。
senses.why: Setting the needle exactly at one mark: words fixed to a precise position.
senses.whyCN: 把指针精确拨到某个刻度：言语被固定在明确位置上。

senses.title: A tense or excited condition, especially of mind
senses.definition: a particular emotional or mental condition, often agitated
senses.definitionCN: 某种情绪或心理状况，常指焦躁不安的状态
senses.example: She was in a state before the exam results came out.
senses.exampleCN: 考试成绩公布前她紧张极了。
senses.why: The needle trembles off its calm mark when feelings run high.
senses.whyCN: 情绪高涨时指针离开平静刻度而颤抖，成为「紧张状态」。

intro.en: State came through Old French from Latin status, a noun of standing, and grew both political and verbal senses.
intro.cn: state 经古法语源自拉丁语 status（站立之姿），发展出政治义与动词义。

items.en: Status, from stare meaning to stand, was the manner of standing or the position of things.
items.cn: 拉丁语 status 来自动词 stare（站立），指事物所处的姿态或位置。

items.en: Estat meant condition, rank, and position, borrowed into English with the s kept from Latin.
items.cn: 古法语 estat 意为状况、等级与地位，进入英语时保留了拉丁语的 s。

items.en: State at first meant condition or rank, as in estate and the state of affairs.
items.cn: 进入英语后最初指状况、等级，如 estate 与 the state of affairs。

items.en: The political sense grew: the state as the body politic, later the American states.
items.cn: 16 世纪政治义兴起：指政治共同体「国家」，后指美国的州。

items.en: The verb to state, shortened from state as in state one's case, became standard for formal saying.
items.cn: 动词 to state 从正式陈述用法中定型，成为「说明；规定」的标准动词。

note.en: State shares a root with estate and statue, and sits near words for condition and country of different roots.
note.cn: state 与 estate、statue 同根，义场又靠近词源不同的若干「状况」「国家」词。

entries.definition: a large area of land, or all the money and property someone owns
entries.definitionCN: 地产；遗产；与 state 同源于拉丁语 stare

entries.definition: a carved or cast figure of a person or animal
entries.definitionCN: 雕像；同源于「站立」之意，立起来的人像

entries.definition: a person's natural height, or their importance and reputation
entries.definitionCN: 身高；声望；同根词，原义站立的高度

entries.definition: the state that someone or something is in, especially health or fitness
entries.definitionCN: 状况；条件，强调具体健康或运行情况

entries.definition: the social or professional position of someone at a time
entries.definitionCN: 地位；身份；与 state 同源，偏重社会位置

entries.definition: a large group of people sharing a country and culture
entries.definitionCN: 国家；民族，强调人群与文化，与强调政治组织的 state 有别

entries.definition: a large administrative area of a country
entries.definitionCN: 省；行政区，与自治程度较高的 state 不同

normalIntro.en: Use the shared stand-root family and the real collocations to lock the senses.
normalIntro.cn: 利用共享的「站立」词根家族与真实搭配来锁定各义项。

normal.en: Latin stare means to stand, so a state is where something stands.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 stare 意为站立，state 就是事物「立在哪」的状况。

normal.en: Estate, statue, and stature all come from the same stand-root.
normal.cn: estate、statue、stature 都源自同一「站立」词根。

normal.en: The State Department shows the government sense in a famous name.
normal.cn: 美国国务院 The State Department 体现了「国家；政府」义。

normal.en: As stated above is a set phrase for referring back in writing.
normal.cn: as stated above 是书面语中回指前文的固定说法，体现动词义。

normal.en: In a state idiomatically means upset or agitated.
normal.cn: 习语 in a state 表示「紧张不安」，对应第 5 个义项。

abstract.en: Picture a row of gauges, each needle showing where things currently stand.
abstract.cn: 想象一排仪表盘，每根指针都标示着当前的状况。

abstract.en: See a country run like one ordered machine with the word State on its panel.
abstract.cn: 把国家想成一台有序运转的机器，面板上写着 State。

abstract.en: Feel your own needle trembling before exam results, needle off its mark.
abstract.cn: 体会公布成绩前自己指针离位颤抖的心情。

examples.en: The report states clearly that the river water is unsafe.
examples.cn: 报告明确说明河水不安全。

examples.en: The building was sold because of its terrible state.
examples.cn: 这栋楼因状况糟糕而被出售。

examples.en: Each American state sets its own driving laws.
examples.cn: 美国每个州都有各自的驾驶法规。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯铁特」——像铁轨上一个固定的停靠点，火车停在哪里就是它此刻的状态。

root: 拉丁语 stare（站立）派生名词 status（所立之处、姿态），经古法语 estat 进入英语；词族含 estate、statue、stature、status 等，均含「立定、定位」的核心意象。

sensesIntro.en: The stand-root image opens into the condition of things, the nation as one ordered body, its regional parts, the act of fixing words precisely, and a trembling mental condition.
sensesIntro.cn: 「站立定位」的意象展开为：事物的状况、作为整体的国家、其组成部分「州」、把话说定到精确位置的动词义，以及心绪失衡的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle fixed at a reading, where something stands
core.cn: 核心意象：指针停在某个读数上，标示事物立定之处

branches.en: the condition something or someone is in, calm or agitated
branches.cn: 人或事物所处的状况，平静或紧张

branches.en: the political body and its regional parts
branches.cn: 政治共同体及其组成单元「州」

branches.en: setting words at an exact point
branches.cn: 把言语精确固定在某一位置上

branches.en: the needle resting at its true reading
one machine panel read as a whole nation
branches.cn: 整块机器面板被读作一个国家

intro.en: The stand-root family shows one Latin verb branching into nouns for standing, standing figures, and standing places.
intro.cn: 「站立」词根家族展示了一个拉丁动词如何派生出关于立定、立像、立处的一批名词。

latinIntro.en: From Latin stare, to stand, come several English words that keep the sense of fixed position.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stare（站立）派生出多个保留「固定位置」义的英语词。

items.structure: Latin status via Old French estat
items.meaning: condition; political body; to say formally
a written law formally set down
to say again in different or the same words

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「陈述；声明」
由 re- 加本词构成，义为「重申；重新表述」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「庄严的；气派的」

definition_zh: 统计数值；统计数据；（statistics）统计学；统计资料
definition_en: a single number giving measured information, or statistics, the science of collecting and studying such numbers
core_image: 一张布满格子的表格，每个格子里坐着一个被数出来的数字
scene: 人口普查的办公室里，调查员整理成摞问卷。Each statistic in the census report came from thousands of questionnaires.
sceneCN: 这里 statistic 是「统计数值」（第 1 个义项：由数据算出的一个数字）；句意为普查报告中的每个统计数字都来自数千份问卷。

pos.zh: 名词：统计数值；统计数字

collocations.zh: 能说明问题的统计数字

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「统计的；统计学的」
由本词加指人后缀构成，义为「统计学家；统计员」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「统计上；按统计来看」

senses.title: A single number giving measured information
senses.definition: one number that represents a fact measured or counted from data
senses.definitionCN: 由数据测量或计数得出的、代表某一事实的一个数字
senses.example: One sad statistic is that most new cafés close within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 一个令人遗憾的统计数字是，多数新咖啡馆在一年内关门。
senses.why: One cell of the big table holds one counted number.
senses.whyCN: 大表格里的一个格子装着一个被数出来的数字。

senses.title: Statistics, the science of collecting and studying numbers
senses.definition: the study of collecting, organizing, and interpreting numerical data, usually as the plural subject statistics
senses.definitionCN: 收集、整理和解释数字数据的学科，通常以复数形式 statistics 指这门学科
senses.example: She is studying statistics at university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学里学习统计学。
senses.why: The whole table, not one cell, becomes the field of study itself.
senses.whyCN: 当整张表格而不是单个格子成为研究对象，就成了一门学科。

senses.title: Statistics, a set of numerical facts collected together
senses.definition: a collection of numerical facts about a subject, such as population or prices
senses.definitionCN: 关于某一主题（如人口或物价）汇总起来的成套数字事实
senses.example: Tourism statistics for the year were published in March.
senses.exampleCN: 该年度的旅游统计资料于三月发布。
senses.why: Many filled cells laid side by side form a body of facts.
senses.whyCN: 许多填好的格子并排排列，汇成一套事实资料。

intro.en: Statistic grew from the idea of the state's science: numbers first collected for governments to govern by.
intro.cn: statistic 源于「国家的科学」：数字最初是为政府治国而收集的。

items.en: Statisticum collegium, a 17th-century term, meant a council concerned with state affairs.
items.cn: 17 世纪新拉丁语 statisticum collegium 指研究国事的学问团体。

items.en: Statista meant a person skilled in statecraft, dealing with facts of the state.
items.cn: 意大利语 statista 指精通国政之人，处理与国家有关的事实。

items.en: Statistik, coined in the 18th century, meant the analysis of state data such as population and land.
items.cn: 18 世纪德语 Statistik 指对国家数据（人口、土地等）的分析。

items.en: Statistics entered English first as state data, then widened to any numerical science of data.
items.cn: statistics 进入英语时先指国家数据，后扩展为泛指的数据科学。

items.en: The singular statistic settled for one number, while statistics names both the science and collected data.
items.cn: 单数 statistic 定型为「一个统计数值」，statistics 兼指学科与统计资料。

note.en: Statistic shares its state-root with state and status, and sits near words of different roots for measured facts.
note.cn: statistic 与 state、status 同含「国家」词根，义场又靠近词源不同的若干「数据事实」词。

entries.definition: a political country, a condition, or to say something formally
entries.definitionCN: 国家；状态；陈述；与 statistic 同含「国家」词根

entries.definition: the social or professional position of someone
entries.definitionCN: 地位；身份；同根词，源自「站立、立国」意象

entries.definition: a place where trains stop, or where someone is posted
entries.definitionCN: 车站；驻地；同根词，原义「立定之处」

entries.definition: a number, especially one shown in official records
entries.definitionCN: 数字；数额，泛指数字本身，不强调统计方法

entries.definition: facts or information used for calculating or analyzing
entries.definitionCN: 数据；资料，是统计前的原始材料

entries.definition: an official count of a population
entries.definitionCN: 人口普查，是产生统计数值的典型来源

entries.definition: a standard of measurement used for judging performance
entries.definitionCN: 指标；度量标准，强调用于衡量的规则

normalIntro.en: Anchor the word to its state-root family and the real subject name statistics.
normalIntro.cn: 把单词锚定在「国家」词根家族和学科名 statistics 上。

normal.en: The root stat- means state: numbers first collected for governments.
normal.cn: 词根 stat- 意为「国家」：数字最早为政府而收集。

normal.en: Statistics is the school subject name, always plural.
normal.cn: statistics 是学科名称，始终用复数形式。

normal.en: State, status, station, and statistic all carry the same stat- root.
normal.cn: state、status、station、statistic 都带同一 stat- 词根。

normal.en: A statistician is the person who works with statistics.
normal.cn: statistician 是与统计打交道的人，即统计学家。

normal.en: Statistically significant is a fixed phrase in research writing.
normal.cn: statistically significant（统计上显著）是研究写作的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture one glowing cell in a giant spreadsheet, holding a hard-won number.
abstract.cn: 想象巨型表格中一个发光的格子，装着一个来之不易的数字。

abstract.en: See a clerk long ago counting people for the king, the first statistic.
abstract.cn: 想象古代书吏为国王清点人口，那是最早的统计数字。

abstract.en: Feel the whole table turn into a classroom subject called statistics.
abstract.cn: 体会整张表格变成一门叫统计学的课堂科目。

examples.en: The jobless rate is a statistic that changes every month.
examples.cn: 失业率是每月都在变化的统计数字。

examples.en: Behind every statistic is a family with a story.
examples.cn: 每个统计数字背后都有一个有故事的家庭。

examples.en: Statistics can mislead when the sample is too small.
examples.cn: 样本太小时，统计结果可能造成误导。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯的提斯蒂克」——谐音「死记的题是提分的题」：把一堆数字死记住、统计好就能提分。

root: 源自拉丁语 status（国家；所立之姿），经意大利语 statista 与德语 Statistik 进入英语；与 state、station、status 同根，核心意象是「为立国而收集的数字」。

sensesIntro.en: From one counted cell of state data, the idea grows into the whole science of numbers and the collected body of facts.
sensesIntro.cn: 从国家数据表格中的一个格子，展开为整门数字科学以及汇总成套的统计资料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one counted number sitting in a cell of the state's great table
core.cn: 核心意象：国家大表格的格子里坐着一个被数出来的数字

branches.en: a single number measured from data
branches.cn: 由数据得出的单个数字

branches.en: the science of numbers as a subject
a collected set of numerical facts
cells filled and laid side by side
the whole table taught in a classroom
branches.cn: 整张表格走进课堂成为学科

intro.en: The stat- family shows how a root for the state grew numbers, positions, and standing figures.
intro.cn: stat- 词族展示「国家」词根如何派生出数字、地位与立定之物。

latinIntro.en: From Latin status, the state and manner of standing, several English words descend.
latinIntro.cn: 多个英语词源自拉丁语 status（国家；所立之姿）。

items.meaning: the science or the collected data

items.structure: same root via Old French estat

items.meaning: relating to a practice or system
items.meaningCN: 形容词后缀，表与某体系相关

items.meaning: makes nouns for a person skilled in something

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「统计的」

definition_zh: 地位；身份；状况；情形；职位
definition_en: the social, professional, or legal position of a person or thing at a time
core_image: 胸前别着的一枚徽章——别人一眼看出你站在哪一排
scene: 公司年会上，新头衔牌被摆上座位。Her promotion gave her a new status in the company hierarchy.
sceneCN: 这里 status 是「地位；身份」（第 1 个义项：人在社会或组织中的位置）；句意为她的晋升使她在公司层级中获得了新地位。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加拉丁语成分构成的固定短语，义为「现状」
由本词加复合成分构成的短语，义为「身份的象征；彰显地位之物」

senses.title: A person's standing in society or an organization
senses.definition: the relative social or professional rank of a person
senses.definitionCN: 人在社会或职业中的相对等级
senses.example: Doctors enjoy high status in many countries.
senses.exampleCN: 医生在许多国家享有很高的地位。
senses.why: The badge pinned on the chest tells everyone which row you stand in.
senses.whyCN: 胸前的徽章告诉所有人你站在哪一排，即等级位置。

senses.title: The official condition of a person or thing in law or a system
senses.definition: the recognized legal or administrative condition of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或制度中被认可的法定情形
senses.example: The refugees were granted official status to stay.
senses.exampleCN: 这些难民获得了留居的正式身份。
senses.why: The badge issued by an office, not earned by crowds: a fixed registration.
senses.whyCN: 徽章不是靠人望挣来而是由机构颁发：一次固定登记。

senses.title: The current situation or condition at a given time
senses.definition: the present state of progress or affairs, as in status update
senses.definitionCN: 某事当前的进展或情形，如状态更新
senses.example: The pilot checked the status of all systems before takeoff.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员起飞前检查了所有系统的状态。
senses.why: A machine's badge is its row of indicator lights, read at a glance.
senses.whyCN: 机器的「徽章」是一排指示灯，一眼读出当前情形。

intro.en: Status is a straight borrowing of Latin status, the manner of standing, which also gave English state.
intro.cn: status 直接借自拉丁语 status（站立之姿），英语 state 亦同源。

items.en: A reconstructed root *sta- meant to stand.
items.cn: 重构词根 *sta- 意为「站立」。

items.en: Status, from the verb stare, meant the way one stands: condition and position.
items.cn: 拉丁语 status 源自动词 stare，指站立的方式：状况与位置。

items.en: In learned 17th-century usage, status meant legal condition, as in status in re publica.
items.cn: 17 世纪学术用语中，status 指法律身份。

items.en: English took status first for legal and diplomatic standing, later for social rank generally.
items.cn: 英语先用于法律与外交身份，后泛指社会地位。

items.en: Digital life added the sense of a system's current condition, as in status update.
items.cn: 数字时代增加了系统当前状态之义，如 status update。

note.en: Status is a Latin cousin of state and statute, and sits near different-root words for rank and condition.
note.cn: status 与 state、statute 是拉丁同源表亲，义场又靠近词源不同的等级、状况词。

entries.definition: a carved or cast figure that stands upright
entries.definitionCN: 雕像；与 status 同源于「站立」，只是拼读相近易混

entries.definition: a written law formally fixed
entries.definitionCN: 成文法令；同根词，原义「被立定之物」

entries.definition: a person's height or their moral importance
entries.definitionCN: 身高；声望；同根词，源自站立的高度

entries.definition: a position in a scale of importance or in an organization
entries.definitionCN: 等级；职级，强调序列中的位置

entries.definition: respect and admiration earned by success or quality
entries.definitionCN: 威望；声望，强调他人眼中的敬意

entries.definition: a person's reputation or official position
entries.definitionCN: 地位；名望，与 status 同含「站立」意象但词源路径不同

entries.definition: the physical state of something
entries.definitionCN: 状况；状态，偏重实体情况而非社会位置

normalIntro.en: Link status to its stand-root cousins and to real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 把 status 与「站立」词根表亲及真实固定短语关联起来。

normal.en: Latin stare means to stand; status is how one stands in a group.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 stare 意为站立，status 就是一人在群体中「立」的位置。

normal.en: Status quo is a Latin phrase meaning the existing situation.
normal.cn: status quo 是拉丁语短语，意为「现状」。

normal.en: Marital status appears on almost every official form.
normal.cn: marital status（婚姻状况）几乎出现在每张表格上。

normal.en: Status update is the standard name for posting your current state online.
normal.cn: status update 是发布个人当前状态的标准说法。

normal.en: Status, state, statue, and statute share the same stand-root.
normal.cn: status、state、statue、statute 共享同一「站立」词根。

abstract.en: Picture rows of people and a badge showing exactly which row is yours.
abstract.cn: 想象一排排人群，胸前徽章标出你属于哪一排。

abstract.en: See an airplane dashboard where each light reports a system's status.
abstract.cn: 看飞机仪表盘上每盏灯汇报一个系统的状态。

abstract.en: Feel the stillness of a statue standing, fixed where it was placed.
abstract.cn: 体会雕像静静立定、被固定在原处的静感。

examples.en: The new title raised her status within the team.
examples.cn: 新头衔提高了她在团队中的地位。

examples.en: Please indicate your marital status on the form.
examples.cn: 请在表格上注明婚姻状况。

examples.en: The app shows the status of your order in real time.
examples.cn: 应用会实时显示订单状态。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯代特斯」——谐音「时代特设」：每个时代都特设一套身份地位。

root: 直接借自拉丁语 status（stare「站立」的派生名词），核心意象是「所立之位」；与 state、statue、statute 同根，词根一般认为可上溯至印欧语 *sta-（站立）。

sensesIntro.en: The standing-place image covers social rank, official registration, and a system's present reading.
sensesIntro.cn: 「所立之位」的意象涵盖社会等级、法定登记与系统的当前读数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a badge showing the row where someone stands
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚徽章，标出人站立的那一排

official legal or administrative standing
a system's current condition
the badge issued or earned
a row of indicator lights read at a glance

intro.en: Status belongs to the wide stand-root family, where every word fixes something in place.
intro.cn: status 属于庞大的「站立」词族，每个词都把某物固定在位置上。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare, to stand, produced status and its English cousins.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stare（站立）派生出 status 及其英语同族词。

items.structure: same root via Old French estat

items.meaning: a law set down in writing

items.structure: Latin phrase, the state in which

definition_zh: 稳定的；平稳的；持续的；（使）稳住；（使）镇定
definition_en: not moving, changing, or shaking; continuing regularly; to make something firm or calm
core_image: 一只手稳稳托住摇晃的水杯——杯中的水面不再颤动
scene: 桥面被风吹得轻轻晃动，工友伸手扶住架子。He held the ladder steady while his partner climbed up.
sceneCN: 这里 steady 是动词「使稳住」（第 4 个义项：让某物不晃动）；句意为同伴爬梯时他把梯子扶稳了。

pos.zh: 形容词：稳定的；平稳的；持续的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「平稳地；持续地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「稳定；沉稳」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「不稳的；摇晃的」

senses.title: Firmly fixed, not shaking or moving
senses.definition: held or fixed firmly so that it does not shake or wobble
senses.definitionCN: 被牢牢固定、不摇晃不摆动的
senses.example: Keep the camera steady while you take the picture.
senses.exampleCN: 拍照时保持相机稳定。
senses.why: The hand under the cup stops the water surface from trembling.
senses.whyCN: 托住杯子的手让水面不再颤动，即固定不动。

senses.title: Continuing regularly without sudden change
senses.definition: continuing or developing gradually and evenly over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间平稳均匀地延续或发展
senses.example: The company has shown steady growth for five years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司连续五年稳步增长。
senses.why: The cup that never spills month after month: no sudden tilts.
senses.whyCN: 那只月月不洒的杯子：没有突然的倾斜，即均匀延续。

senses.title: Reliable and calm in character
senses.definition: describing a person who is calm, sensible, and reliable
senses.definitionCN: 形容人冷静、明理、可信赖
senses.example: She is a steady worker who never loses her temper.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个沉稳的员工，从不发脾气。
senses.why: A person who never tilts is trusted the way a firm shelf is trusted.
senses.whyCN: 从不倾斜的人像结实的架子一样被人放心倚靠。

senses.title: To make something firm or stop it shaking
senses.definition: to hold or support something so that it stops moving or shaking
senses.definitionCN: 扶住或支撑某物使其停止晃动
senses.example: He steadied the wobbly table with a folded newspaper.
senses.exampleCN: 他用折起的报纸垫稳了摇晃的桌子。
senses.why: The hand itself goes under the cup: the image turns into an action.
senses.whyCN: 那只手主动伸到杯子下面：意象由状态转为动作。

senses.title: To make someone calm after shock or fear
senses.definition: to help someone become calm again after being frightened or upset
senses.definitionCN: 帮助受惊或心绪不宁的人恢复平静
senses.example: She took a deep breath to steady herself before speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 开口前她深吸一口气让自己镇定下来。
senses.why: Steadying the shaking cup of one's own feelings.
senses.whyCN: 把自己那只情绪之杯扶稳，即让内心不再晃动。

intro.en: Steady comes from stead, the old word for a standing place, plus an adjective ending: fixed in its place.
intro.cn: steady 源自古语 stead（立定之位）加形容词后缀，本义是「固定在其位置上」。

items.en: A reconstructed root *stad- meant to stand or stay fixed.
items.cn: 重构词根 *stad- 意为站立、固定不动。

items.en: Stede meant a place or standing spot, surviving today in stead and instead.
items.cn: 古英语 stede 指地点、立身之处，今存于 stead 与 instead 中。

items.en: Stedfast and stedi described things fixed in their place, firm and unwavering.
items.cn: 中古英语 stedfast、stedi 描述固定在原位、坚定不动之物。

items.en: Steady widened to regular behaviour and dependable character, and became a verb.
items.cn: steady 扩展出「规律、可靠」之义，并发展出动词用法。

items.en: The verb covers both steadying objects and calming people, while go steady named steady courtship.
items.cn: 动词兼指扶稳物件与安抚人心，go steady 则指确定恋爱关系。

note.en: Steady belongs to the stand-place family with stead and instead, and sits near different-root words for firm and calm.
note.cn: steady 与 stead、instead 同属「立定之位」词族，义场又靠近词源不同的「牢固」「镇定」词。

entries.definition: the place or role of someone or something, as in in his stead
entries.definitionCN: 替代之位；与 steady 同根，是本词的名词源头

entries.definition: in the place of something else
entries.definitionCN: 代替；反而；同根复合词，义为「立于其位」

entries.definition: a horse ridden by a knight, a literary word
entries.definitionCN: 坐骑；骏马；拼读相近但词源不同，属文学用语

entries.definition: firmly fixed and not likely to change or fall
entries.definitionCN: 牢固的；稳定的，与 steady 同含「站立」意象且词源相近

entries.definition: solid, strongly fixed, and not moved easily
entries.definitionCN: 坚固的；坚决的，强调不易被动摇

entries.definition: happening all the time or staying the same
entries.definitionCN: 恒定的；不断的，强调持续不变

entries.definition: moving unsteadily from side to side
entries.definitionCN: 摇晃的；不稳的，与 steady 意义相反

normalIntro.en: Use the stead place-root and the real verb patterns to hold each sense firm.
normalIntro.cn: 利用 stead「地点」词根与真实动词搭配把各义项稳稳记住。

normal.en: Steady grows from stead, a standing place, so it means fixed in place.
normal.cn: steady 由 stead（立身之地）生长而来，本义即固定在位。

normal.en: Instead is in stead, in the place of something else, same root.
normal.cn: instead 即 in stead（立于其位），同一词根。

normal.en: Hold steady and steady yourself are the two main verb patterns.
normal.cn: hold steady 与 steady yourself 是两大动词句式，分别指物与人。

normal.en: Go steady is an informal phrase for a steady boyfriend or girlfriend.
normal.cn: go steady 是口语说法，指确定恋人关系。

normal.en: Steadily is the adverb seen in steadily rising prices.
normal.cn: 副词 steadily 常见于 steadily rising prices（价格稳步上涨）。

abstract.en: Picture a hand sliding under a trembling cup until the water surface stills.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手垫到颤动的杯子下面，直到水面静止。

abstract.en: See a growth line on a chart rising evenly, never jumping or dipping.
abstract.cn: 看图表上一条均匀上升的增长线，从不跳升或骤跌。

abstract.en: Feel your own breath slowing to steady yourself before a hard talk.
abstract.cn: 体会艰难谈话前靠呼吸把自己稳住的感受。

examples.en: Prices rose at a steady pace through the summer.
examples.cn: 整个夏天物价平稳上涨。

examples.en: She steadied the bike while the child got on.
examples.cn: 孩子上车时她扶稳了自行车。

examples.en: He is a steady friend who never lets you down.
examples.cn: 他是从不让你失望的可靠朋友。

sensesIntro.en: From a thing fixed in its place grow the even passage of time, a reliable character, the act of holding firm, and calming a shaking heart.
sensesIntro.cn: 由「固定在位」生长出时间的均匀延续、可靠的品格、扶稳的动作与安抚人心的用法。

core.cn: 核心意象：一只手垫在颤动的杯下，直到水面静止

scene: 生日晚上，餐厅铁板端上桌还冒着白烟。He ordered a medium-rare steak with pepper sauce for his birthday dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 steak 是「牛排」（第 1 个义项：厚切的烤肉块）；句意为他生日晚餐点了一份五分熟牛排配胡椒酱。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加复合成分构成，义为「牛排馆」
由 beef 加本词构成的复合词，义为「牛排；牛排番茄」

senses.title: A thick slice of beef cooked by grilling or frying
senses.definition: a thick flat piece of beef, usually grilled or fried and served whole
senses.definitionCN: 一块厚而平的牛肉，通常整块烤制或煎制后上桌
senses.example: The chef grilled the steak over charcoal for six minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师用炭火把牛排烤了六分钟。
senses.why: One thick slab cut straight from the animal, cooked on its own.
senses.whyCN: 从整块肉上直切下来的厚板，独自受火而成。

senses.title: A thick slice of other meat or fish
senses.definition: a similar thick piece cut from pork, lamb, tuna, salmon, or other flesh
senses.definitionCN: 从猪肉、羊肉、金枪鱼、三文鱼等切下的类似厚块
senses.example: She pan-fried a tuna steak with lemon and herbs.
senses.exampleCN: 她用平底锅煎了一块配柠檬香草的金枪鱼排。
senses.why: The same slab shape, cut from another body.
senses.whyCN: 同样的厚板形状，只是取自另一副躯体。

senses.title: Minced beef used for pies and stews
senses.definition: beef cut into small pieces for slow cooking, as in steak and kidney pie
senses.definitionCN: 切成小块用于慢炖的牛肉，如牛肉腰子派
senses.example: He bought steak for the winter stew at the butcher's.
senses.exampleCN: 他在肉铺买了炖冬季浓汤用的牛肉块。
senses.why: The slab broken down into small squares for the long pot.
senses.whyCN: 厚板被改刀成小块，投入需要久煨的锅里。

intro.en: Steak comes from an Old Norse word for a thick slice roasted on a stick or spit.
intro.cn: steak 源自古诺斯语，指串在签或烤叉上的厚肉片。

items.en: A reconstructed root *staik- meant to stick or pierce, related to pointed objects.
items.cn: 重构词根 *staik- 意为穿刺、签插，与尖物相关。

items.en: Steik meant a thick piece of meat roasted on a spit.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 steik 指串在烤叉上炙烤的厚肉块。

items.en: Steike entered English through northern dialects for a slice of meat for roasting.
items.cn: 中古英语 steike 经北方方言进入英语，指用于烤制的肉片。

items.en: Spelling settled as steak, and the word covered slices of beef chiefly.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 steak，词义以牛肉切片为主。

items.en: The word widened to fish steaks and minced stewing beef, and steakhouse was formed.
items.cn: 词义扩展到鱼排与炖用牛肉块，并衍生出 steakhouse 一词。

note.en: Steak looks like the unrelated stake, and sits near different-root words for cut meat.
note.cn: steak 拼写上与不相关的 stake 相近，义场靠近词源不同的切肉词。

entries.definition: a pointed wooden post, or money risked in a bet
entries.definitionCN: 木桩；赌注；与 steak 只是发音相同，词源不同

entries.definition: a thin branch or a narrow rod
entries.definitionCN: 棍；枝条；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a neat pile of things placed one on another
entries.definitionCN: 堆；垛；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a small piece of meat cut with part of the rib bone
entries.definitionCN: 排骨；带骨肉块，切法与部位与牛排不同

entries.definition: a thin slice of meat, often coated and fried
entries.definitionCN: 肉饼；炸肉片，较薄且常裹粉

entries.definition: a boneless piece of meat or fish
entries.definitionCN: 去骨的肉片或鱼片，强调无骨

entries.definition: a large piece of meat cooked whole in an oven
entries.definitionCN: 整烤的大块肉，比牛排大得多

normalIntro.en: Separate steak from stake by meaning, and learn the cut-word field together.
normalIntro.cn: 先区分 steak 与 stake，再把「切肉」词场一起记牢。

normal.en: Steak and stake sound the same: one you eat, one you drive into the ground or bet.
normal.cn: steak 与 stake 同音：一个能吃，一个插地或作赌注。

normal.en: Old Norse steik meant meat roasted on a spit, keeping the stick idea.
normal.cn: 古诺斯语 steik 指烤叉上的肉，保留了「签插」意象。

normal.en: Tuna steak and salmon steak show the fish sense.
normal.cn: tuna steak、salmon steak 展示了鱼排之义。

normal.en: Steak and kidney pie is the famous British stew dish.
normal.cn: steak and kidney pie（牛肉腰子派）是著名的英式炖菜。

normal.en: A steakhouse is a restaurant famous for steak.
normal.cn: steakhouse 是以牛排闻名的餐厅。

abstract.en: Hear the sizzle as a thick slab hits the iron plate.
abstract.cn: 听厚肉块贴上铁板时的滋滋声。

abstract.en: See the smoke rise from a charcoal grill at an open window.
abstract.cn: 看临街窗口炭烤架上腾起的烟。

abstract.en: Picture a knight's spit turning slowly over the fire, meat on a stick.
abstract.cn: 想象骑士时代的烤叉在火上缓缓转动，肉串在签上。

examples.en: She cooks the steak for three minutes on each side.
examples.cn: 她把牛排每面煎三分钟。

examples.en: This restaurant is famous for its grilled steak.
examples.cn: 这家餐厅以烤牛排闻名。

examples.en: A tuna steak needs only a short time in the pan.
examples.cn: 金枪鱼排在锅里只需煎一小会儿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯贴克」——谐音「死贴锅」：牛排死死贴住热锅，滋滋作响。

root: 一般认为源自古诺斯语 steik（烤叉上的厚肉片），词根可上溯至日耳曼语 *staik-（刺、插，与签棒相关）；与同音的 stake（木桩；赌注）词源不同。

sensesIntro.en: From the spit-roasted slab grow slices of beef, thick cuts of other flesh and fish, and the small pieces saved for the stew pot.
sensesIntro.cn: 由叉烤厚板生长出牛排、其他肉与鱼的厚切排，以及留作炖锅的小肉块。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick slab of meat sizzling on iron or spit
core.cn: 核心意象：厚肉块在铁板或烤叉上滋滋作响

branches.en: the classic thick beef cut
the same slab from fish or other meat
branches.cn: 取自鱼或其他肉的同形厚块

branches.en: small beef squares for the slow pot
whole cuts served straight to the plate
the slab broken down for long cooking

intro.en: Steak is a short root word with few derivatives, joined mainly into eating compounds.
intro.cn: steak 是个短词根词，派生词少，主要参与构成饮食类复合词。

latinIntro.en: Steak has no Latin relatives; it came from Old Norse, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: steak 没有拉丁同源词，源自古诺斯语，故拉丁同族词列表为空。

items.meaning: a thick slice of meat or fish

items.exampleCN: 市中心一家老牌牛排馆

items.meaning: a sharp table knife for cutting steak
a thick slice of beef; also a large tomato type
a pointed post or money risked
items.meaningCN: 木桩；赌注（与 steak 无关）

items.meaning: a thin slice of meat for frying
makes nouns for a place of business

definition_zh: 偷；窃取；剽窃；偷偷地走；（棒球）盗垒；便宜货
definition_en: to take something that belongs to someone else without permission, or to move quietly
core_image: 黑暗里一只手无声地伸进别人的口袋——东西换了主人却无人察觉
scene: 美术馆的警报在深夜响起，巡警逐层搜查。Thieves tried to steal a famous painting from the museum last night.
sceneCN: 这里 steal 是「偷；窃取」（第 1 个义项：未经许可拿走他人之物）；句意为昨夜窃贼企图从博物馆偷走一幅名画。

collocations.phrase: a real steal at this price

derivatives.zh: 与本词相关的名词，义为「偷窃；盗窃（罪）」
与本词相关的指人名词，义为「小偷；贼」
与本词同源，义为「偷偷摸摸；隐秘行动」
由本词过去分词转作形容词，义为「被偷的」

senses.title: To take something that is not yours
senses.definition: to secretly take something that belongs to another person without permission
senses.definitionCN: 未经许可悄悄拿走属于他人的东西
senses.example: Someone stole her wallet on the crowded bus.
senses.exampleCN: 有人在拥挤的公交车上偷了她的钱包。
senses.why: The hand goes into the pocket without the owner's eyes seeing.
senses.whyCN: 那只手伸进口袋，而主人的眼睛看不见，即无声地易主。

senses.title: To take someone's ideas or words as your own
senses.definition: to use another person's ideas, words, or work and claim them as your own
senses.definitionCN: 把别人的想法、话语或成果据为己有
senses.example: The rival company stole their design for the new phone.
senses.exampleCN: 对手公司窃取了他们的新手机设计。
senses.why: The same hidden hand, reaching into the mind instead of the pocket.
senses.whyCN: 同一只隐形之手，只是伸进的是头脑而非口袋。

senses.title: To move quietly and secretly
senses.definition: to go somewhere quietly, so that no one notices you
senses.definitionCN: 悄悄地前往某处，不让人察觉
senses.example: The cat stole across the room toward the sleeping bird.
senses.exampleCN: 猫悄悄穿过房间，逼近睡着的鸟。
senses.why: The thief's walk: footsteps shaped by not being seen.
senses.whyCN: 贼的脚步：为了不被看见而塑造出的步态。

senses.title: To gain attention unfairly or unexpectedly
senses.definition: to attract all the attention in a situation, as in steal the show
senses.definitionCN: 在某个场合吸引全部注意力，如 steal the show
senses.example: The little girl stole the show at the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼上小姑娘抢尽了风头。
senses.why: Attention, like property, is quietly taken from its rightful holders.
senses.whyCN: 注意力如财物一样被悄悄从应得者手中拿走。

senses.title: To buy something at a surprisingly low price
senses.definition: a bargain so good that it feels like getting something for almost nothing, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 便宜得近乎白拿的好交易，作名词使用
senses.example: At fifty dollars, this coat is a steal.
senses.exampleCN: 这件大衣五十美元，真是捡漏。
senses.why: So cheap it feels like the price itself was stolen.
senses.whyCN: 便宜到仿佛价格本身被偷走了。

intro.en: Steal is an ancient Germanic word for taking secretly, from a root also seen in stealth.
intro.cn: steal 是古老的日耳曼词，指偷偷拿取，与 stealth（隐秘）同根。

items.en: A reconstructed root *steul- meant to take secretly, giving thief and stealth as cousins.
items.cn: 重构词根 *steul- 意为暗中拿取，其同源词有 thief 与 stealth。

items.en: Stelan meant to steal, already with the full sense of secret taking.
items.cn: 古英语 stelan 意为偷窃，已具备「暗中拿取」的完整词义。

items.en: Stelen kept the meaning, and the irregular past stole and stolen fixed their forms.
items.cn: 中古英语 stelen 沿用原义，不规则过去式 stole、stolen 逐渐定型。

items.en: The quiet movement sense grew from the thief's walk, as in steal away.
items.cn: 由贼的步态生长出悄悄移动之义，如 steal away。

items.en: Sporting uses (steal a base) and the bargain noun became common in American English.
items.cn: 体育用法（盗垒）与「便宜货」名词在美式英语中流行开来。

note.en: Steal looks like the unrelated steel, and its real family hides in stealth and thief.
note.cn: steal 拼写上与不相关的 steel 相近，真正的同族词藏在 stealth 与 thief 中。

entries.definition: a hard strong metal made from iron and carbon
entries.definitionCN: 钢；与 steal 发音相同、只差一个字母，词源不同

entries.definition: not moving; continuing until now
entries.definitionCN: 静止的；仍然；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: the quality of moving secretly so no one notices
entries.definitionCN: 隐秘；偷偷摸摸；与 steal 同根，是它的名词亲戚

entries.definition: to take money or property from a person or place by force or threat
entries.definitionCN: 抢劫；掠夺，强调对人或场所下手，常带强制

entries.definition: to steal small things repeatedly, often from one's workplace
entries.definitionCN: 小偷小摸；监守自盗，指反复偷取小物

entries.definition: to steal something small, a British informal word
entries.definitionCN: 顺手牵羊；偷拿（英式口语）

entries.definition: to give something back to its owner
entries.definitionCN: 归还；送还，与偷取方向相反

normalIntro.en: Keep steal and steel apart, and grow memory from the stealth family.
normalIntro.cn: 区分 steal 与 steel，再从 stealth 词族延伸记忆。

normal.en: Steal, stole, stolen is the irregular verb chain to memorize.
normal.cn: steal—stole—stolen 是需要记住的不规则动词链。

normal.en: Steel the metal has an e for the metal, steal the crime has e and a like take and give.
normal.cn: 钢 steel 只含 e；偷 steal 含 e 和 a，联想 take（拿）与 give（给）。

normal.en: Stealth bombers fly with the same root: secret movement.
normal.cn: 隐形轰炸机 stealth bomber 用同一个词根：隐秘行动。

normal.en: Steal the show and steal a glance show the widened senses.
normal.cn: steal the show 与 steal a glance 体现扩展义项。

normal.en: A steal as a noun means a great bargain in shopping talk.
normal.cn: 名词 a steal 在购物语境中指超值的便宜货。

abstract.en: See a hand slip into a pocket in the dark, silent as shadow.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中一只手滑进口袋，静如影子。

abstract.en: Hear soft cat footsteps crossing a quiet floor at night.
abstract.cn: 听猫在深夜安静地板上悄然走过。

abstract.en: Feel the crowd's eyes swing to the child who stole the show.
abstract.cn: 体会全场目光被抢镜的孩子夺走的瞬间。

examples.en: Bikes are often stolen around the station, so lock yours well.
examples.cn: 车站附近常丢自行车，务必锁好。

examples.en: He stole a glance at his watch during the meeting.
examples.cn: 开会时他偷偷看了一眼手表。

examples.en: Her idea was stolen and published under another name.
examples.cn: 她的想法被人剽窃，用别人的名字发表了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯提尔」——谐音「死提」：小偷死死盯住别人的东西，提了就跑。

root: 源自古英语 stelan（偷），一般认为上溯至日耳曼语 *steul-（暗中拿取）；同源词有 stealth（隐秘）、thief（贼）；与 steel（钢）完全不同源。

sensesIntro.en: From the secret hand in the pocket grow the theft of ideas, the thief's quiet walk, the snatched spotlight, and the bargain so cheap it feels stolen.
sensesIntro.cn: 从口袋里那只隐秘之手生长出剽窃思想、贼的悄然行走、抢走的目光与便宜得像偷来的交易。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a silent hand taking what another hand holds
core.cn: 核心意象：一只无声的手拿走另一只手握着的东西

branches.en: things and ideas taken without asking
branches.cn: 不打招呼拿走的财物与思想

branches.en: the thief's own way of walking
attention taken from its owners
branches.cn: 从应得者处抢走的注意力

branches.en: a price that feels like theft in reverse
branches.cn: 像反向偷窃一样的低价

branches.en: the pocket as the classic scene
branches.cn: 口袋作为经典作案场景

intro.en: Steal keeps its family in native Germanic words, each showing one face of secret taking.
intro.cn: steal 的同族词保存在日耳曼本土词汇中，各自展现「暗中拿取」的一面。

latinIntro.en: Steal has no Latin relatives; it is native Germanic, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: steal 没有拉丁同源词，属日耳曼本土词源，故拉丁同族词列表为空。

items.meaning: taken by theft; past participle of steal
items.meaningCN: 被偷的；steal 的过去分词

items.meaning: the act or crime of stealing
makes nouns of quality or action
items.meaningCN: 本土名词后缀，表性质或行为

derivatives.zh: 与本词同族的名词，义为「偷窃；盗窃（罪）」
与本词同族的指人名词，义为「小偷；贼」
与本词同源，义为「隐秘；偷偷行动」
由本词过去分词转作形容词，义为「被偷的」

definition_zh: 蒸汽；水汽；蒸；冒热气；（喻）精力；势头
definition_en: the hot mist that water becomes when it boils, or to cook with this mist
core_image: 锅盖边缘升起的一缕白汽，把盖子顶得哒哒作响
scene: 早餐铺的蒸笼一层层摞起，白汽漫过街角。Dumplings in the bamboo baskets cook slowly in the rising steam.
sceneCN: 这里 steam 是名词「蒸汽」（第 1 个义项：水沸腾时冒出的热气）；句意为竹笼里的包子在升腾的蒸汽中慢慢蒸熟。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「蒸锅；汽船」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「充满水汽的；闷热的」
由本词现在分词转作形容词，义为「热气腾腾的」

senses.title: The hot mist from boiling water
senses.definition: the white cloud of hot gas that rises from water at boiling point
senses.definitionCN: 水达到沸点时升起的白色热气团
senses.example: Steam poured out when she lifted the pot lid.
senses.exampleCN: 她掀开锅盖时蒸汽涌了出来。
senses.why: The white breath pushing up from the boiling pot and rattling its lid.
senses.whyCN: 从沸腾的锅里向上顶出、把锅盖震得作响的白色气息。

senses.title: To cook food with steam
senses.definition: to cook food over or in boiling steam without putting it in water
senses.definitionCN: 利用沸腾的水汽蒸煮食物，而不直接浸水
senses.example: Steam the fish with ginger for ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼加姜蒸十分钟。
senses.why: Letting the pot's breath do the cooking gently.
senses.whyCN: 让锅里的气息温和地完成烹煮。

senses.title: To give off steam or be covered with it
senses.definition: to produce steam, or to become covered with a film of hot mist
senses.definitionCN: 冒出蒸汽，或被热气蒙上一层水雾
senses.example: The bathroom windows steamed up during her shower.
senses.exampleCN: 她淋浴时浴室的窗户蒙上了水汽。
senses.why: The mist lands on cold glass and blurs the world behind it.
senses.whyCN: 水汽落在冷玻璃上，把身后的世界变得模糊。

senses.title: Power, energy, or forward drive
senses.definition: energy or progress, used in phrases like run out of steam
senses.definitionCN: 精力或进展，用于 run out of steam 等短语
senses.example: The project lost steam after the budget was cut.
senses.exampleCN: 预算削减后，项目失去了势头。
senses.why: The engine's driving mist becomes a person's driving energy.
senses.whyCN: 推动机器的白汽化作推动人的精力。

intro.en: Steam goes back to an Old English word for vapor or smoke, whose older root may mean to be thick or cloudy.
intro.cn: steam 源自古英语表示蒸气、烟气的词，更早的词根一般认为有「浓、浑」之义。

items.en: A reconstructed root *staum- is thought to mean vapor or cloudy mass.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *staum- 意为蒸气或浑浊之团。

items.en: Steam meant vapor or exhalation, covering smoke and steam alike.
items.cn: 古英语 steam 指蒸气、呼出之气，兼指烟。

items.en: Steam kept the vapor sense but narrowed mostly to water vapor.
items.cn: 中古英语沿用蒸气义，但主要收窄为水汽。

items.en: The steam engine made the word central to industry and travel.
items.cn: 18 世纪蒸汽机的出现使该词成为工业与交通的核心词。

items.en: Cooking, bathing, and metaphorical energy senses grew around the industrial core.
items.cn: 在工业本义周围生长出烹调、洗浴与精力比喻诸义。

note.en: Steam shares one letter more with steel and sits near mist words of different roots.
note.cn: steam 与 steel 仅差一个字母，义场靠近词源不同的「雾气」词。

entries.definition: a hard strong metal made from iron and carbon
entries.definitionCN: 钢；与 steam 仅差一个字母，词源不同

entries.definition: to take something secretly without permission
entries.definitionCN: 偷；与 steam 发音相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a literary word for a riding horse
entries.definitionCN: 骏马；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a gas-like form of a substance, especially water in the air
entries.definitionCN: 水汽；蒸气，是更一般化的科学说法

entries.definition: a thin cloud of tiny water drops in the air
entries.definitionCN: 薄雾；水雾，温度较低、成滴成雾

entries.definition: to heat liquid until it bubbles and turns to steam
entries.definitionCN: 煮沸；沸腾，是产生蒸汽的过程

entries.definition: to become solid because of cold

normalIntro.en: Tie steam to the kettle image and to the famous phrases that carry its power sense.
normalIntro.cn: 把 steam 与水壶意象及承载「势头」义的著名短语绑定。

normal.en: The steam engine is the historical heart of the word.
normal.cn: 蒸汽机 steam engine 是这个词的历史核心。

normal.en: Run out of steam means to lose energy like an old engine.
normal.cn: run out of steam 指像旧引擎一样失去动力。

normal.en: Let off steam means to release built-up pressure, like a valve.
normal.cn: let off steam 指像阀门放汽一样宣泄积压的情绪。

normal.en: Steamed vegetables keep more vitamins than boiled ones.
normal.cn: 蒸蔬菜比水煮的保留更多维生素，体现烹调义。

normal.en: Steamed-up windows show the mist-on-glass image.
normal.cn: steamed-up windows（蒙上水汽的窗）体现玻璃结雾的画面。

abstract.en: Watch the kettle lid rattle on a puffing white cloud.
abstract.cn: 看水壶盖被一团团白汽顶得哒哒作响。

abstract.en: Feel a hot shower turning the mirror blind with mist.
abstract.cn: 体会热水澡把镜子蒙得雾白一片。

abstract.en: Sense an old engine slowing down, puffing weaker and weaker.
abstract.cn: 感受老引擎渐渐泄劲，喷出的汽越来越弱。

examples.en: Steam rose from the bowl of hot noodles.
examples.cn: 热气从那碗面条上腾起。

examples.en: She prefers to steam fish rather than fry it.
examples.cn: 她做鱼宁愿清蒸不愿煎炸。

examples.en: After two hours of arguing, the team was out of steam.
examples.cn: 争论两小时后，团队已精疲力竭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯提姆」——谐音「死提吗」：水汽顶着锅盖死命往上提，锅盖直响。

sensesIntro.en: From the pot's rising white breath grow gentle cooking, misty windows, and the engine's power inside a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 从锅中升起的白汽生长出温和的蒸煮、蒙雾的窗，以及引擎般的人之精力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: white breath lifting a rattling pot lid

cooking with the rising breath
mist landing on cold glass
the engine's drive as human energy
branches.cn: 引擎动力化作人的精力

branches.en: the cloud in the air and on surfaces
branches.cn: 空气中与器物表面的白汽

intro.cn: steam 的派生词不多但常用，均保留热气意象。

scene: 大桥工地昼夜施工，钢梁一根根吊装到位。Workers welded thick steel beams to complete the new bridge frame.

pos.zh: 动词：使坚强；使硬起心肠

senses.title: The hard metal made from iron and carbon
senses.definition: a strong hard metal alloy of iron and a small amount of carbon
senses.definitionCN: 由铁与少量碳合成的坚硬金属合金
senses.example: The tower's frame is built of steel, not wood.
senses.exampleCN: 这座塔的骨架是钢制的，不是木头的。
senses.why: Iron that has passed through fire and come back harder.
senses.whyCN: 经过火焰淬炼后变得更坚硬的铁。

senses.title: The steel industry or products of steel
senses.definition: the industry that makes steel, or goods made of it
senses.definitionCN: 生产钢铁的产业，或钢铁制成的产品
senses.example: Her father worked his whole life in steel.
senses.exampleCN: 她父亲一辈子在钢铁行业工作。
senses.why: The metal stands for the whole furnace-and-factory world behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这种金属代表了其背后整个炉火与工厂的世界。

senses.title: Great firmness of will or character
senses.titleCN: 钢铁般的意志；冷酷坚定
senses.definition: firm determination or coldness, as in nerves of steel
senses.definitionCN: 坚定的决心或冷静的强硬，如 nerves of steel
senses.example: She faced the interview with nerves of steel.
senses.exampleCN: 她以钢铁般的意志面对面试。
senses.why: The quenched blade becomes the steadiness of a mind.
senses.whyCN: 淬过火的刀刃化为心境的沉着坚定。

senses.title: To make yourself determined and unfeeling
senses.definition: to prepare yourself mentally to face something difficult or painful
senses.definitionCN: 在心理上做好准备去面对艰难或痛苦之事
senses.example: He steeled himself before opening the test results.
senses.exampleCN: 打开考试成绩前，他硬起了心肠。
senses.why: Quenching your own heart as the smith quenches steel.
senses.whyCN: 像铁匠淬钢一样淬炼自己的心。

intro.en: Steel is an Old English metal word, likely from a root meaning to stand firm or be fixed, related to German Stahl.
intro.cn: steel 是古英语金属词，一般认为源自表示「立定、固定」的词根，与德语 Stahl 同源。

items.en: A reconstructed root *stahla- or *stakh- is thought to mean to be firm or fixed.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *stahla- 或 *stakh- 意为坚定、固定。

items.en: Stele or style meant steel, the hardened metal of weapons and tools.
items.cn: 古英语 stele/style 指钢，即武器与工具用的硬质金属。

items.en: Steel named the metal, its weapons, and hardness in battle metaphors.
items.cn: 中古英语 steel 指金属、兵器，并进入战斗比喻表示坚硬。

items.en: Industry made steel a world word: furnaces, railways, and ships were built of it.
items.cn: 工业时代使 steel 成为世界性词汇：炉窑、铁路与轮船皆以钢筑成。

items.en: The verb steel yourself and adjectives like steely carry the hardness into character.
items.cn: 动词 steel yourself 与形容词 steely 把坚硬意象带入品格领域。

note.en: Steel is only one letter away from steal, and sits near different-root words for metals and hardness.
note.cn: steel 与 steal 仅差一个字母，义场靠近词源不同的金属与坚硬词。

entries.definition: to take something secretly without permission
entries.definitionCN: 偷；与 steel 发音相同、只差一个字母，词源不同

entries.definitionCN: 蒸汽；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: an English surname spelled with an extra e
entries.definitionCN: 英语姓氏；拼法相近，非普通名词

entries.definition: a heavy magnetic metal from which steel is made
entries.definitionCN: 铁；是钢的原材料

entries.definition: a light, very strong metal used in aircraft
entries.definitionCN: 钛；更轻更强的现代金属

entries.definition: firm determination to do something
entries.definitionCN: 决心；坚定，对应 steel 的意志义

entries.definition: to make or become less strong
entries.definitionCN: 削弱；变弱，与使坚强相反

normalIntro.en: Keep steel apart from steal, and anchor the will-sense in the smithy image.
normalIntro.cn: 区分 steel 与 steal，并用铁匠铺意象锚定「意志」义。

normal.en: Steel the metal, steal the crime: one letter changes the story.
normal.cn: steel 是金属，steal 是罪行：一个字母改写故事。

normal.en: Stainless steel is the everyday kitchen form of the metal.
normal.cn: 不锈钢 stainless steel 是厨房里的日常形态。

normal.en: Nerves of steel is a fixed phrase for great calm under pressure.
normal.cn: nerves of steel 是固定说法，指高压下的镇定。

normal.en: Steel yourself means to harden your heart before a hard moment.
normal.cn: steel yourself 指在艰难时刻来临前硬起心肠。

normal.en: Steely describes a cold grey look, like steel itself.
normal.cn: steely 形容冷灰色的目光，如同钢本身。

abstract.en: Watch a red-hot blade hiss as it hits cold water and harden.
abstract.cn: 看烧红的刀刃淬入冷水，嘶声中变硬。

abstract.en: See grey beams rising into a bridge frame at dawn.
abstract.cn: 看黎明中灰色钢梁升起，接成大桥骨架。

abstract.en: Feel your jaw set and your breath slow as you steel yourself.
abstract.cn: 体会硬起心肠时牙关咬紧、呼吸放缓。

examples.en: The kitchen knives are made of stainless steel.
examples.cn: 这些厨刀由不锈钢制成。

examples.en: Steel output in the region doubled in ten years.
examples.cn: 该地区钢产量十年间翻了一倍。

examples.en: She steeled herself for the bad news.
examples.cn: 她做好了心理准备迎接坏消息。

hardness in metal and in mind

definition_zh: 陡峭的；陡直的；（价格等）过高的；浸泡；浸渍
definition_en: rising or falling quickly over a short distance, or to leave something in liquid to soak
core_image: 一面几乎垂直的岩壁立在山路上——向上看去帽子都会掉
scene: 徒步到半山，向导指着前方的岩壁示意大家抓稳。The path became so steep that we had to use ropes near the top.
sceneCN: 这里 steep 是形容词「陡峭的」（第 1 个义项：短时间内急速升降）；句意为接近山顶时坡度陡得我们不得不借助绳索。

pos.zh: 形容词：陡峭的；（价格）过高的

collocations.zh: 浸透着历史；富有历史底蕴

senses.title: Rising or falling quickly over a short distance
senses.definition: sloping sharply upward or downward, hard to climb or walk
senses.definitionCN: 坡度急剧向上或向下，难以攀爬或行走
senses.example: They climbed the steep slope with both hands on the rocks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们双手抓着岩石攀上陡坡。
senses.why: The wall-like slope that forces your body almost flat against it.
senses.whyCN: 近乎墙壁的斜坡逼得人身体几乎贴上去。

senses.title: Too high, especially of prices or demands
senses.definition: unreasonably high, as an amount of money or a demand
senses.definitionCN: 指金额或要求高得不合理
senses.example: Two hundred yuan for a bowl of noodles is a bit steep.
senses.exampleCN: 一碗面两百块有点贵得离谱。
senses.why: The price climbs as suddenly as the rock wall.
senses.whyCN: 价格像岩壁一样陡然爬升，令人望而生畏。

senses.title: To leave something in liquid to soak
senses.definition: to keep food, leaves, or other material in liquid so flavor or substance is drawn out
senses.definitionCN: 把食物、茶叶等泡在液体中使味道或成分释出
senses.example: Steep the dried mushrooms in warm water for half an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 把干香菇在温水里泡半小时。
senses.why: The leaf sinks down a steep drop into the water and stays.
senses.whyCN: 叶子陡然沉入水底并停留其中，即浸泡。

senses.title: Deeply filled with or influenced by something
senses.definition: deeply involved in or shaped by something, as steeped in tradition
senses.definitionCN: 深受某事物浸润或影响，如 steeped in tradition
senses.example: The old quarter is steeped in history and legend.
senses.exampleCN: 老城区浸透着历史与传说。
senses.why: Soaked so long in the liquid of tradition that its color fills everything.
senses.whyCN: 在传统的汁液中泡得足够久，颜色浸透了每个角落。

intro.en: The steep of slopes and the steep of soaking are two ancient roots that happen to share a spelling.
intro.cn: 「陡峭」的 steep 与「浸泡」的 steep 是两个恰好同形的古老词根。

items.en: One reconstructed root *staipa- is thought to mean steep or sharp; another *staup- meant to push under liquid.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *staipa- 意为陡、尖；另一词根 *staup- 意为按入液体。

items.en: Steep meant high and sharp-sloped; steap (verb) meant to dip into liquid.
items.cn: 古英语 steep 指高耸陡斜；动词 steap 指浸入液体。

items.en: Both words kept their forms and senses side by side.
items.cn: 中古英语中两个词形义并存，并行发展。

items.en: The price sense grew as a metaphor of the sharp climb; steeped in took the soaking image into character.
items.cn: 价格义由「陡升」比喻而来；steeped in 把浸泡意象带入品格。

items.en: Tea-making fixed the everyday verb, while steep prices and steep learning curves stayed common.
items.cn: 泡茶固定了日常动词用法，steep prices 与 steep learning curves 仍是常用表达。

note.en: Steep looks like the unrelated step, and sits near slope words and soak words of different roots.
note.cn: steep 拼写上与不相关的 step 相近，义场靠近词源不同的坡度词与浸泡词。

normal.cn: steep price 与 steep hill 共享「陡然爬升」意象。

normal.cn: steep the tea 是泡茶叶的日常动词说法。

由本词加复合成分构成，义为「垫脚石；跳板」

senses.title: A single movement or sound of one foot
senses.definition: one movement of lifting and putting down a foot, or the sound of this
senses.definitionCN: 抬脚落下的一个动作，或由此产生的声响
senses.example: She recognized her mother's quick step in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 她一听就知道走廊里是母亲轻快的脚步声。
senses.why: One flat board of movement: lift, place, done.
senses.whyCN: 一块移动的平板：抬起、落下，一次完成。

senses.title: A flat surface for the foot, as on stairs
senses.definition: one of the flat surfaces you place your foot on to climb stairs or step over
senses.definitionCN: 楼梯上供落脚的平面，或跨越用的踏板
senses.example: Mind the broken step at the bottom of the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 注意楼梯最下面那级破损的台阶。
senses.why: The board itself, fixed where a foot must land.
senses.whyCN: 那块固定在落脚处的板子本身。

senses.title: One stage in a process or series of actions
senses.definition: one action in a series leading to a result, or a stage of progress
senses.definitionCN: 通向结果的一系列动作中的一步，或进展的一个阶段
senses.example: Follow the recipe step by step and the cake will rise.
senses.exampleCN: 按菜谱一步一步来，蛋糕就会发起来。
senses.why: Each landing surface leads to the next, like stairs to a door.
senses.whyCN: 每块落脚板都通向下一块，如楼梯通往门口。

senses.title: A short distance or a marked degree of change
senses.definition: a short distance measured by one stride, or a small degree of difference
senses.definitionCN: 一步跨出的短距离，或程度上的小小差异
senses.example: The bakery is just a few steps from the station.
senses.exampleCN: 面包店离车站只有几步路。
senses.why: The distance one board-length of a foot can cover.
senses.whyCN: 一步之板所能跨越的距离。

senses.title: To move by lifting one foot and putting it down
senses.definition: to put a foot somewhere or move in this way, as in step aside
senses.definitionCN: 把脚踏上某处或如此移动，如 step aside
senses.example: He stepped over the puddle and hurried on.
senses.exampleCN: 他跨过水坑，匆匆前行。
senses.why: The board image becomes the act of placing the foot.
senses.whyCN: 平板意象化为安放脚掌的动作。

intro.en: Step is an Old English word for the sole of the foot and its movement, from a root of pressing or stamping.
intro.cn: step 源自古英语，指脚掌及抬脚落地的动作，一般认为出自「踩踏、按压」词根。

items.en: A reconstructed root *stap- is thought to mean to stamp or press with the foot.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *stap- 意为以足踩踏、按压。

items.en: Steppes meant the soles of the feet; steppe (verb) meant to step or go.
items.cn: 古英语 steppes 指双脚脚掌；动词 steppe 意为迈步、行走。

items.en: Step covered the movement, its sound, the stair surface, and the measure of distance.
items.cn: 中古英语 step 兼指动作、声响、楼梯踏板与距离单位。

items.en: The process sense grew: every step of the way, step by step.
items.cn: 过程义发展起来：every step of the way、step by step。

items.en: Compounds like stepfather and stepping-stone spread the word into family and progress images.
items.cn: stepfather、stepping-stone 等复合词把该词带入家庭与「垫脚石」意象。

note.en: Step looks almost identical to the unrelated steep, and its real family lies in steppe-like Germanic ground words.
note.cn: step 与不相关的 steep 拼写几乎一样，其真正词族在于日耳曼语的地面类词。

entries.definition: sloping sharply upward or downward
entries.definitionCN: 陡峭的；与 step 只差一个字母，词源不同

entries.definition: to come to or make an end of movement
entries.definitionCN: 停止；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a vast level treeless grassland in Eurasia
entries.definitionCN: 大草原；与 step 同音异源，源于草原民族语言

entries.definition: a single step or the speed of walking
entries.definitionCN: 步伐；步速，强调节奏与速度

entries.definition: a long decisive step
entries.definitionCN: 大步；阔步，比 step 更长更有力

entries.definition: one part of a process or development
entries.definitionCN: 阶段；时期，对应 step 的过程义

entries.definition: an action taken to achieve a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 措施；举措，与 step 的「措施」义相近

normalIntro.en: Use the stair image to hold movement, surface, and process in one picture.
normalIntro.cn: 用楼梯画面把动作、踏板、过程三者收进一幅图。

normal.en: Step by step is the fixed phrase for careful progress.
normal.cn: step by step（一步步地）是表达循序渐进的固定短语。

normal.en: Watch your step warns about both stairs and situations.
normal.cn: watch your step 既提醒楼梯安全，也提醒处世谨慎。

normal.en: Stepfather and stepmother use step for family ties by marriage.
normal.cn: stepfather、stepmother 用 step 表示因再婚而结成的亲属关系。

normal.en: Stepped is the regular past form, unlike steep, which is an adjective.
normal.cn: stepped 是规则过去式；而 steep 是形容词，注意区分。

normal.en: A stepping-stone is the classic metaphor for a means to an end.
normal.cn: stepping-stone（垫脚石）是经典的「达成手段」比喻。

abstract.en: Climb one stair board at a time, hand on the rail.
abstract.cn: 扶着扶手，一次踩上一级楼梯。

abstract.en: Hear an old wooden stair creak under slow feet.
abstract.cn: 听老旧木楼梯在缓慢脚步下的吱呀声。

abstract.en: See each process move to its next labeled stage, like climbing floors.
abstract.cn: 看流程逐级推进，像楼层被逐层登临。

examples.en: He stepped back to let the crowd pass.
examples.cn: 他退后一步让人群通过。

examples.en: Learning a language is a matter of small daily steps.
examples.cn: 学语言靠的是每天一小步的积累。

examples.en: The first step of the plan is to find funding.
examples.cn: 计划的第一步是找到资金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯代普」——谐音「死台阶」：一级级死板的台阶，只能一步一步往上踩。

root: 源自古英语 steppes（脚掌）、steppe（迈步），一般认为上溯至日耳曼语 *stap-（踩踏）；与 steep、stop 无词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: From one footfall grow the stair board under it, the stages of any process, the short distance of a stride, and the verb of placing a foot.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一次落脚生长出脚下踏板、过程的阶段、一步的距离，以及安放脚掌的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one flat board where a foot lands on its way up
core.cn: 核心意象：上行途中一块供脚掌落脚的平板

branches.en: the movement and the sound of feet
the fixed surface that receives the foot
boards of a process, one after another
the distance one stride covers
a measure taken toward a result

intro.en: Step compounds freely, marking both family ties and pieces of the path upward.
intro.cn: step 能自由构成复合词，既标记姻亲关系，也标记上行路径的组成部分。

latinIntro.en: Step has no Latin relatives; it is native Germanic, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: step 没有拉丁同源词，属日耳曼本土词源，故拉丁同族词列表为空。

items.meaning: a footfall; a stair surface; a stage
the sound or mark of a step
the father of one's parent by remarriage
a stone to step on; a means to an end

items.meaningCN: 大草原（与 step 异源）

items.meaning: one of a series of steps
marks ongoing action; can form adjectives
a child of one's spouse by an earlier marriage

derivatives.zh: 由本词加复合成分构成，义为「继父」
由 foot 加本词构成，义为「脚步；足迹」
